# Design system

Plain CSS, a theme script and a component script, with no build step. The tokens and
components make a screen look right; `GUIDELINES.md` decides what goes on it. This skill
carries the whole system; `VERSION` names the design-system commit it was packaged from.

## Before building any UI

1. Read `GUIDELINES.md` in full. It is short, and the no-go list in section 10 is
   mostly the things generated UI gets wrong by default. Don't work from memory of it.
2. For each element you need, grep its class in `references/elements.html` (app
   elements, with the reason beside each) or `references/index.html` (foundations and
   assembled patterns) and copy that markup.
3. Grep `assets/ds/ds.css` before writing any new CSS. If a class or token does the job,
   use it. Never a raw hex, a one-off margin or a font weight outside the tokens.

## Adding it to an app

Copy `assets/ds/` into the app's static folder as `ds/`, then load, in this order:
`ds/theme.js` in `<head>` with no `defer`, `ds/ds.css`, the app's own stylesheet, and
`ds/components.js` at the end of `<body>`. The copied files are never edited in the app;
app-specific styles go in the app's own stylesheet. The first line of `ds.css` names the
commit it came from, so to update an app, compare it with `VERSION` and copy again.

For a single-file page or artifact, inline `ds.css`, `theme.js` and `components.js`.
The fonts then fall back to system fonts unless they are embedded too.

hindsight keeps its own colours (a recorded exception); everything else applies to it.

## Changing the system itself

Not here: this skill is generated. Changes go to the design-system repo
(https://github.com/valentinwerner1/design-system), where tests guard the tokens and
pushing to main repackages this skill. A gap you find while building an app (a missing
state, a component two apps both need) goes there too, not into the app's CSS.

## Before calling a screen done

Go through the checklist in `GUIDELINES.md` section 11, in the browser, not from the
code: both themes, reduced motion, keyboard, 320px wide. Its last item, the test run,
applies only in the design-system repo.
